title: Scalable oversight of superhuman systems
bottleneck: As models exceed human capability in a domain, humans can no longer reliably judge their outputs — the supervisor becomes the bottleneck. A doctor cannot evaluate a superhuman diagnostician; a programmer cannot review superhuman code. Proposed solutions like debate and amplification extend human judgment but don't fundamentally solve it: past some capability gap, the AI can fool any human-based check. Even AI-assisted evaluation inherits the problem recursively: the assistant must itself be trusted at the capability frontier.
why_it_blocks: Training and deployment both depend on evaluation. If we can't evaluate superhuman work, we can't train it safely or catch its mistakes.
current_state: Labs use AI-assisted evaluation and debate protocols experimentally. No publicly demonstrated method guarantees reliable oversight of systems smarter than their overseers.
